title: Find a Target Using Linear Search
description: Read N integers, then a target value. Print the zero-based index of the first occurrence of the target, or -1 if it is not present.
input_format: First N (1 ≤ N ≤ 1000), then N integers, then the target integer.
output_format: Print the zero-based index of the first matching element, otherwise -1.

starter_code.Python:
n = int(input())
numbers = list(map(int, input().split()))
target = int(input())
answer = -1
for index in range(n):
    if numbers[index] == target:
        answer = index
        break
print(answer)

learning_content.title: Linear search
learning_content.intro: Linear search checks elements from left to right until it finds the target or reaches the end of the array. The first matching position is returned.
points: Read N and the N array values.
Compare each value with the target.
Stop at the first match; if no match exists, keep the answer as -1.
learning_content.note: In the worst case, every element is inspected.

quiz.question: If the target appears at indexes 1 and 4, which index should this task return?

options.feedback: The task requests the first occurrence, which is at index 1.
Index 4 is a later occurrence, not the first one.
The task uses zero-based indexes, not the one-based position.
A matching target is present, so -1 is not appropriate.

quiz.explanation: Linear search stops at the first match, and indexes are zero-based.
